title: The Student Who Sued Pepsi For A Fighter Jet
sources: Leonard v. PepsiCo, Inc., 88 F. Supp. 2d 116 (S.D.N.Y. 1999) — 1995/1996 Pepsi Stuff commercial joked a Harrier fighter jet cost 7,000,000 Pepsi Points.
Wikipedia / CBS News — Business student John Leonard collected 15 Pepsi Points, raised funds to mail a $700,008.50 check at 10 cents per extra point, and demanded the ~$23M-$37M military jet.

lines.text: In 1996, one college student actually tried to buy a real fighter jet from Pepsi.
lines.caps: In 1996, | one college student | actually tried | to buy a real | fighter jet | from Pepsi.

lines.text: And he had the check to prove it.
See, Pepsi aired a flashy commercial offering prizes for Pepsi Points.
At the end, a teenager flew a Harrier jet to school,
lines.caps: At the end, | a teenager | flew a | Harrier jet | to school,

lines.text: with a joke label reading seven million points.
Drinking seven million sodas was impossible.
Except the fine print let buyers purchase extra points for ten cents each,
lines.caps: Except | the fine print | let buyers | purchase | extra points | for ten cents | each,

lines.text: Twenty-one-year-old John Leonard did the math.
He raised seven hundred thousand dollars from rich investors,
mailed fifteen bottle points plus a giant check,
and demanded his twenty-three-million-dollar military jet.
Pepsi panicked, mailed the check back, and ended up in federal court.
A judge ruled nobody buys a fighter jet for soda points,
though Pepsi quickly edited the price to seven hundred million.
